headline: 18.4 billion e-payment transactions in 2025, but 48 e-money issuers face very different economics
context: BNM Annual Report 2025 shows e-payments grew 25% to 18.4 billion in 2025; retail value RM831 billion. DuitNow QR is now the national interoperable standard. The unfinished agenda is consumer protection across 48 licensed e-money issuers.

changes.summary: Correction: the 1,120 Sabah and 1,799 Sarawak ReDI registrations are January to May 2025 figures out of 3,229 nationwide, and the two states made up about 90% of them; earlier editions read them as shares of the 22,368 total and said adoption was stuck.

cards.big: Malaysia made 18.4 billion e-payment transactions in 2025 (538 per Malaysian), but 48 e-money issuers face very different economics
cards.sub: BNM AR 2025: retail e-payment value reached RM831B (up 19%), average e-money transaction rose to RM43 from RM33, DuitNow QR doubled to 3 billion.

cards.big: FATF/APG: Malaysia has 48 licensed e-money issuers. Touch 'n Go reports 24M verified users and profitability since Q3 2024.
cards.sub: Sarawak's S Pay Global runs as a state alternative with about 1.6M registered users, proof local ecosystems can coexist where politics demands.

cards.big: ReDI signed up 22,368 traders for e-wallets by May 2025; Sabah and Sarawak supplied 2,919 of 3,229 who joined from January to May 2025.
cards.sub: JTK Sabah approved TNG eWallet for migrant-worker pay; TNG says over RM3.5B in wages went through it nationwide in 2025. BNM: cash prevails among low-income users.

cards.big: PDPA covers banking with no carve-out, but the consent you sign at signup is the door through which your transaction data flows.
cards.sub: Grab's notice names group companies, marketing partners and credit bureaus as recipients; TNG's names group entities and business partners.

cards.big: The interoperability question is already half-answered: DuitNow QR is the national standard. The harder questions are about fees, BNPL exposure, and who is left out.
Adoption is not protection. The infrastructure works. The guardrails on merchant fees, BNPL supervision, and meaningful consent are still being assembled.
